semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {ذَرْواً}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) of emphasis, governed by its derivative, which is the active participle. The object is omitted for brevity, since there is nothing comparable to what it scatters here. Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza assimilated the «تاء» of «الذاريات» into the «ذال» of «ذَرْواً».

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {وَقْراً}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «بالحاملات». «الوِقْر» with kasra is the name for what is loaded, that is, carried. It was also read «وَقْراً» with fatḥa, on the basis of naming the object by the maṣdar. It is also permissible that it be a maṣdar in its own right, governed by the sense of the preceding verb, since «الحمل» and «الوقر» have one meaning, even if there is generality and specificity between them.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {يُسْراً}: It is permissible that it be a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the sense of what precedes it, that is, «جَرْياً يُسْراً» ("an easy course"), and that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "possessing ease" or "possessing facility", or that they themselves be made ease, for emphasis.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أَمْراً}: It is permissible that it be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is the apparent sense, and that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "that which is commanded"; on this it needs the object of «المُقَسِّمات» to be omitted. It may be said: there is no purpose in implying it, as with «الذَّارِيات». Are these different things, so that the «واو» is used in its usual sense of joining distinct things? For «الذاريات» are the winds, «الحاملات» the ships, «الجاريات» the stars, and «المُقَسِّمات» the angels. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that the wind alone is meant, because it brings the clouds into being, carries them, steers them, and runs in the air with an easy course." I say: on this it would be a joining of attributes while the one meant is single, as in his saying:
4100 - يا لَهْفَ زَيَّابَةَ للحارثِ الصَّا ... بِحِ فالغانِمِ فالآيِبِ
(Alas for Zayyāba, for al-Ḥārith, the dawn-raider, then the one who takes booty, then the one who returns!)
and the saying of another:
4101 - إلى المَلِك القَرْمِ وابْنِ الهُمامِ ... ولَيْثِ الكتيبةِ في المُزْدَحَمْ
(To the noble king, son of the valiant, and lion of the squadron in the press of battle.)
This is an oath, whose answer is His saying: «إنما تُوْعدون».

semin-durr:5-5.t: And «ما» may be a noun (ism), with its returning pronoun omitted, that is, «تُوْعَدونه»; or it may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it has no returning pronoun according to the well-known view. In that case «تُوْعدون» may be derived from «الوَعْد» (promise) or from «الوعيد» (threat), for it can be said «أَوْعَدْتُه فهو يُوْعَد» and «وَعَدْتُه فهو يُوعَد» without difference; so the implied sense is: "Indeed your promise" or "Indeed your threat." There is no need for the saying of those who said that in His saying «لَصادِقٌ» the active participle stands in the place of the maṣdar, that is, «لصِدْقٌ» ("truth"); for the wording of the active participle is more emphatic, since the promise or the threat is made truthful for emphasis, even though the attribute properly belongs to the one who promises or threatens.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {ذَاتِ الحبك}: The majority read «الحُبُك» with two ḍammas, which are the tracks, such as the tracks of sand and water when the wind strikes it; and «حُبُك الشَّعْر» are the marks of its curling and waving. Zuhayr said:
4102 - مُكَلَِلٌ بأصولِ النجم تَنْسُجُه ... ريحُ حَريقٍ لضاحي مائِه حُبُكُ
(Crowned with the roots of the plants, a fierce wind weaves ripples on the exposed face of its water.)
«الحُبُك» is a plural; its singular may be «حَبيكة», like «طريقة» and «طُرُق», or «حِباك», like «حِمار» and «حُمُر». The rajaz poet said:
4103 - كأنَّما جَلَّلها الحُوَّاكُ ... طِنْفِسَةٌ في وَشْيِها حِباكُ
(As if the weavers had covered it with a carpet whose embroidery has woven patterns.)
The root of «الحَبْك» is making a thing firm and well-made, and from this a coat of mail is called «مَحْبوكة». It was also said: «الحَبْك» is tightening and securing. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4104 - قد غدا يَحْمِلُنِي في أَنْفِه ... لاحِقُ الإِطْلَيْنِ مَحْبوكٌ مُمَرّْ
(He set out carrying me on his nose-ridge: a horse lean in the flanks, tightly built, strongly twisted.)
There are many readings of this word. From al-Ḥasan there are six: «الحُبُك» with ḍamma as the majority; «الحُبْك» with ḍamma and sukūn, which is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAmr; «الحِبِك» with kasra on both; «الحِبْك» with kasra and sukūn, which is a lightening of the kasra form; «الحِبَك» with kasra and fatḥa; and «الحِبُك» with kasra and ḍamma. Of these six, the last is the most troubling, because this pattern is unused among Arabic forms. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others said: "It is from talfīq (mixing)", meaning that there are two dialects, kasra on the «حاء» and the «باء», and ḍamma on both; so this reader took the kasra from one dialect and the ḍamma from the other. People found this unlikely, since mixing only occurs between two words. The Shaykh explained it on the basis that the «حاء» was made to follow the vowel of the «تاء» in «ذات»; he said: "He did not count the «لام» as a separator, since it is sukūn, and so it is a weak barrier." Abū Mālik al-Ghifārī agreed with al-Ḥasan on this reading. ʿIkrima read it with ḍamma and fatḥa, as the plural of «حُبْكة», like «غُرْفة» and «غُرَف». Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Mālik read «الحَبَك» with two fatḥas, the plural of «حَبَكة», like «عَقَبة» and «عَقَب». These are eight readings.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {إِنَّكُمْ}: this is the answer to the oath.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ}: an adjective of «قول». The pronoun in «عنه» refers to the Qur'an, or to the Messenger, or to the religion, or to what you are promised, that is, "he is turned away from it". It was also said: «عن» is causal, and the thing turned away from is omitted; the pronoun in «عنه» on this refers to «قولٍ مختلفٍ», that is, "because of the saying, whoever wants Islam is turned away, by someone saying: it is magic, it is soothsaying." The majority read both verbs in the passive. Qatāda and Ibn Jubayr read «يُؤْفَكُ عنه مَنْ أَفَك», the first passive and the second active, that is, "he is turned away from it who turned people away from it." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يَأْفَكُ» in the active, from «أفك الشيء», that is, "he turns people away from it who is himself turned away." From him also: «يَأْفِكُ عنه مَنْ أَفَّك» with shadda, that is, "who is himself a great liar." It was also read «يُؤْفَنُ عنه مَنْ أُفِنَ» with «نون» in both, that is, "he is deprived of it who is deprived", from «أَفِنَ الضَّرْعَ» when one exhausts it by milking.

semin-durr:10-10.t: It was also read «قَتَل» in the active, the subject being Allah the Exalted, with «الخَرَّاصين» as its object.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدين}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It was said: both are adverbials, so how can one adverbial occur within another? The reply: it is on the basis of an omitted event, that is, "when is the occurrence of the day", so «أيَّان» is an adverbial for the occurrence. The reading «إيَّان» with kasra was mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ هُمْ}: It is permissible that it be accusative by an implied element, that is, "the recompense will come on the day when they...". It is also permissible that it be a badal (substitute) from «يومُ الدين», the fatḥa being a fatḥa of indeclinability (binā') according to the view of those who allow the adverbial to be indeclinable even when annexed to a nominal clause. On this it would be a report of the meaning of their words, spoken in mockery; had it come as a report of their earlier wording, it would have been said: «يومَ نحن على النار نُفْتَنُ». And «يوم» is accusative by «الدين». It was also said: by an implied verb, that is, «يَحارون» ("they will be bewildered"). It was also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied «أعني» ("I mean"). «يُفْتَنون» is made transitive by «على» because it has the sense of "being tested". It was also said: «على» has the sense of «في». It was also said that «يومَ هم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, «هو يومَ هم», with the fatḥa for the reason given. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Zaʿfarānī, «يومُ هم» with nominative, and it likewise supports the view of badal. A similar matter was discussed in Ghāfir.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {ذُوقُواْ}: that is, "it is said to them: Taste." And «هذا الذي كنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); this is the apparent sense. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that «هذا» be a badal (substitute) from «فِتْنتكم», because it has the sense of punishment.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {آخِذِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in His saying «جناتٍ». And «ما آتاهم» means from what is in Paradise, so it is a true ḥāl. It was also said: what He gave them of His commands and prohibitions in this world, in which case it is a reported ḥāl, because of the difference of the two times. He made the prepositional phrase here the khabar (predicate) and the adjective an addition, and reversed this in His saying {إِنَّ المجرمين فِي عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدُونَ} [الزخرف: 74]. It was said: because the khabar is the point of the sentence. The aim there is to report their eternal stay, because the believer may enter the Fire, but he must come out of it. As for the verse of the God-fearing, He made the adverbial the khabar for their security of not leaving it, making that the focus of the benefit so that they obtain reassurance; so the adjective became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {كَانُواْ قَلِيلاً}: There are several views. The first: that the sentence is complete at «قليلاً»; for this reason some paused at «قليلاً» to match His saying {وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ} [ص: 24] and {وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِيَ الشكور} [سبأ: 13], and began {مِّن الليل مَا يَهْجَعُونَ}, that is, "what they sleep of the night." This is not clear in meaning or in grammar. As to the first, they must sleep, and a negation of their sleeping cannot be conceived. As to grammar, what lies within the scope of a negation does not precede it according to the Basrans; this is if you take «ما» as negative; and if you take it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle, the implied sense becomes "of the night is their sleeping", which has no benefit, since all other people are the same.
The second: that «ما» is a maṣdar particle in the position of nominative by «قليلاً». The implied sense: "their sleeping was little".
The third: that the maṣdar «ما» is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from the ism of kāna, that is, "their sleeping was little"; and «من الليل» on these two views is not attached to «يَهْجَعون», because what lies in the scope of the maṣdar does not precede it according to the well-known view; some of those who forbid it excuse it in the case of an adverbial, so it is allowed according to them, while the forbidder implies a verb indicated by «يَهْجَعون», that is, "they slept of the night".
The fourth: that «ما» is redundant and «يَهْجَعون» is the khabar of kāna. The implied sense: "they slept of the night a little sleep," or "a little time"; so «قليلاً» is an adjective of a maṣdar or of an adverbial.
The fifth: that it has the sense of «الذي», with its returning pronoun omitted, the implied sense being: "they were a little of the night, the time in which they sleep"; and this involves strain.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {وبالأسحار}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسْتَغْفرون». The «باء» has the sense of «في». What is attached to the khabar (predicate) is put before the mubtadaʾ (subject), since it is permissible to bring the governing element forward.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {وفي أَنفُسِكُمْ}: a conjunction (nasaq) on «في الأرض», so it is also a khabar (predicate) for «آياتٌ». The implied sense: "in the earth and in yourselves are signs." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Whoever makes it nominative by the adverbial makes the pronoun of the signs be in the adverbial." He means whoever makes the agent nominative by the adverbial absolutely, that is, even if it does not rest on something before it, makes this preposition raise an agent which is the pronoun of «آياتٌ». Some allowed that it be attached to «تُبْصِرُون», but this is invalid, because the interrogative and the «فاء» prevent it. Qatāda read «آيَةٌ» [الذاريات: 20] in the singular.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying {رِزْقُكُمْ}: that is, "the cause of your provision". Ḥumayd and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «رازِقُكم», an active participle; and Allah the Exalted is far above direction.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
The pronoun in «إنَّه لحقٌّ» is either for the Qur'an, or for the religion, or for the day in His saying {وَإِنَّ الدين لَوَاقِعٌ} [الذاريات: 6], {يَوْمَ هُم} [الذاريات: 13], {يَوْمُ الدين} [الذاريات: 12], or for the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying {مِثْلَ مَا}: the two (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read «مثلُ» with nominative, and there are three views on it. The first: that it is a second, independent khabar (predicate), like the first. The second: that it, together with what precedes it, forms a single khabar, as in «هذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ» ("this is sweet-sour"); Abū al-Baqāʾ reported these two. The third: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «حق»; and «ما» is redundant on all three views. «أنَّكم» is the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), that is, «لَحَقٌّ مثلُ نُطْقِكم» ("a truth like your speaking"). It does no harm to imply its annexation to a definite word, because it does not become definite by that, owing to its vagueness.
The rest read it with accusative, and there are several views on it. The best known: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «حَقٌّ» as in the first reading, and the noun was made indeclinable because of its annexation to something not fully inflected, as the other poet made it indeclinable in his saying:
4105 - فتَداعَى مَنْخِراه بدَمٍ ... مثلَ ما أثمرَ حَمَّاضُ الجَبَلْ
(His two nostrils called to each other with blood, like what the sorrel of the mountain bears as fruit.)
with fatḥa on «مثلَ» though it is a naʿt of «دم»; and as «غيرَ» was made indeclinable in his saying:
4106 - لم يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ منها غيرَ أَن نَطَقَتْ ... حمامةٌ في غُصونٍ ذاتِ أَوْقالِ
(Nothing prevented the drinking from it except that a dove cooed in branches full of foliage.)
where «غيرَ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يَمْنع» and he made it indeclinable on fatḥa because of its annexation to «أنْ نَطَقَتْ». What was said earlier on the reading with fatḥa of {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [الأنعام: 94] spares me from restating this.
The second: that «مثلَ» was compounded with «ما» until the two became one thing. Al-Māzinī said: "Like it are «وَيْحَما», «هَيَّما» and «أَيْنَما»", and he quoted Ḥumayd ibn Thawr:
4107 - ألا هَيَّما مِمَّا لَقِيْتُ وهَيَّما ... ووَيْحاً لِمَنْ لم يَدْرِ ما هُنَّ وَيْحَما
(Ah, such longing from what I have met, such longing! And woe to him who did not know what they are, woe!)
He said: were it not for indeclinability, it would be with tanwīn. He also quoted:
4108 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فأكْرِمْ بنا أُمَّاً وأكْرِمْ بنا ابْنَما
(... How noble through us is a mother, and how noble through us is a son!)
Some grammarians held what he mentioned, and quoted:
4109 - أثورَ ما أَصِيْدُكم أم ثورَيْنْ ... أم هذه الجَمَّاءَ ذاتَ القرنَيْنْ
(Shall I hunt for you a bull, or two bulls, or this hornless one that has two horns?)
But as for his quotation of «وأكرِمْ بنا ابنَما», this does not belong to the topic, because this is «ابن» to which a «ميم» has been added; and when a «ميم» is added to it, the «نون» is made to follow the «ميم» in vowels according to the eloquent usage, so you say «هذا ابنمٌ», «ورأيت ابنَماً», «ومررت بابنِم», with the case vowels falling on the «ميم» and the «نون» following. And «ابنما» in the verse is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), so the fatḥa is due to the accusative, not to indeclinability; and this is not the redundant «ما», rather the «ميم» alone is redundant and the «ألف» is a replacement for tanwīn.
The third: that it is accusative as an adverbial; this is the view of the Kufans, who allow «زيدٌ مثلَك» with fatḥa. Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it from Abū al-Ḥasan, but in a problematic wording; he said: "It is read with fatḥa, and there are two views on it: one, it is inflected, and then there are several views on its accusative." Then he said: "Or that it is nominative in position but was given fatḥa as the adverbial was given fatḥa in His saying {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [الأنعام: 94] according to al-Akhfash." Then he said: "And the second view is that it is indeclinable." Abū ʿUbayd said: "Some Arabs always make «مثل» accusative, saying: «هذا رجلٌ مثلَك»."
The fourth: that it is accusative by dropping the preposition, which is the «كاف» of comparison. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs make it accusative when a noun, meaning the mubtadaʾ, is raised by it, saying: «مثلَ مَنْ عبدُ الله؟», «وعبدُ الله مثلَك», «وأنت مثلَه»; because the «كاف» may enter upon it, so it is made accusative when you drop the «كاف»." I say: there is room for objection in this. What need is there to imply the entering of the «كاف» when «مثل» gives its benefit? It is as if he saw the «كاف» entering upon it in His saying {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ} [الشورى: 11] and said that.
The fifth: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, that is, «لَحَقٌّ حقاً مثلَ نُطْقِكم». The sixth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لَحَقٌّ», because qualifying with this maṣdar has become so frequent that it runs in the course of derived attributes, and the operator on it is «حَقٌّ». The seventh: that it is a ḥāl from «حقٌّ» itself, even though it is indefinite. Sībawayh stated its permissibility in several places in his book, and Abū ʿUmar followed him in that.
This «ما», in a construction like this, as in their saying «هذا حَقٌّ كما أنَّك ههنا» ("this is as true as that you are here"), may not be dropped, so it is not said «هذا حَقٌّ كأنَّك هنا». Al-Khalīl, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, stated this. When you make «مثل» inflected, «ما» is redundant and «أنكم» is in the position of genitive by annexation, as mentioned; and when you make it indeclinable, either by compounding or by its annexation to something not fully inflected, two views are allowed for this «ما»: that it is redundant, and that it is an indefinite noun with an adjective; so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. There is room for objection in it, because of the absence of an adjective here. If he says: it is omitted, then the default is non-omission. Moreover, they have stated that this adjective is not omitted because its qualified noun is vague. As for «أنَّكم تَنْطِقون», it may be genitive by annexation if «ما» is redundant; and if it is indefinite, it is in the position of accusative by an implied «أعني», or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {إِذْ دَخَلُواْ}: There are four views on what governs «إذ». The first: that it is «حديثُ», that is, "has the account of them reached you, occurring at the time of their entering upon him?" The second: that it is accusative by the sense of the verb in «ضَيْف», because originally it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and for this reason the masculine singular and others are alike in it, as if it were said: "those whom he entertained at the time of their entering upon him". The third: that it is accusative by «المُكْرَمين», if by their being honoured is meant that Ibrāhīm honoured them by serving them. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied «اذْكُر» ("remember"); and it is not permissible to make it accusative by «أتاك», because of the difference of the two times.
The majority read «المُكْرَمين» with the «راء» light, from «أكرم»; ʿIkrima read it with shadda.
His saying: {سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ}: its treatment was given earlier in Hūd. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is plausible that «قالوا» governs «سَلاماً», making «سلاماً» in the sense of «قولاً», and the meaning then is: they said a greeting and a saying whose meaning is 'peace'. This is the view of Mujāhid." I say: it would be better to make the implied sense that they said this very wording, and the explanation of this wording is the customary greeting. The differences of the readers over «سلاماً», regarding fatḥa or kasra of its «سين» and sukūn or fatḥa of its «لام», were also mentioned earlier.
The majority read the first «سلاماً» accusative and the second nominative; they were also read both nominative; and it was read «سَلاماً قال: سِلْماً» with kasra on the «سين» of the second and accusative. The justification of all this is not hidden, from what was said in Hūd.
His saying: {قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ}: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); they implied: «أنتم قومٌ». Some did not find this good, because it lacks friendliness, and the like of it would not occur from Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him; so it is better to imply «هؤلاء قومٌ» or «هم قومٌ», and this saying of his would be to the people of his household and his close ones, not to the guest himself, because that would alarm them.

semin-durr:26-26.t: And His saying: {فَجَآءَ}: a conjunction on «فراغَ», and its being caused by it is clear. The hamza in «ألا تأكلون» is for reproach of them for not eating, or an offer, or an urging.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {فِي صَرَّةٍ}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), that is, "being in a cry". «الصَّرَّة» was said to be the shout. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4110 - فَأَلْحَقَنا بالهادياتِ ودونَه ... جَواحِرُها في صَرَّةٍ لم تَزَيَّلِ
(He brought us up with the leaders, and before him the hounds in a throng that did not disperse.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from «صَرَّ الجُنْدُبُ» (the locust chirped), «والبابُ» (the door creaked) and «والقلمُ» (the pen scratched). Its position is accusative as a ḥāl, that is, «فجاءَتْ صارَّةً» (she came crying out)." It is also permissible that it be attached to «أَقْبَلَتْ», that is, "she came forward among a group of women who were with her." «الصَّرَّةُ» is a group of women.
His saying: {فَصَكَّتْ}: that is, she slapped. There was disagreement about it. It was said: it is striking with the hand outstretched. It was also said: rather, it is striking the face with the fingertips, as one does in amazement, and this is the custom of women.
His saying «عجوزٌ»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, «أنا عجوزٌ عقيمٌ فكيف أَلِدُ؟» ("I am an old barren woman, so how can I give birth?"). The other verse explains it.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by the second «قال», that is, "just as the saying we have told you, your Lord has said", meaning that it is from Allah, so do not be amazed at it.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {مُّسَوَّمَةً}: There are three views. The first: that it is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة». The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the preposition phrase before it. The third: that it is a ḥāl from «حجارة», and what made this good is that the indefinite noun was qualified by the prepositional phrase after it.
His saying: {عِندَ رَبِّكَ}: an adverbial for «مُسَوَّمةً», that is, "marked with Him".

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {فِيهَآ آيَةً}: It is permissible that the pronoun refer to the town, that is, "we left in the town a sign, such as the stones or the foul water"; and it is permissible that it refer to the destruction understood from the context.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {وَفِي موسى}: There are several views. The first, which is the apparent one: that it is a conjunction on His saying «فيها» with repetition of the preposition, because what is conjoined to is a genitive pronoun; so it is attached to «تَرَكْنا» in meaning, and the implied sense is: "and we left in the story of Mūsā a sign." This is a clear meaning. The second: that it is conjoined to His saying {وَفِي الأرض آيَاتٌ} [الذاريات: 20], that is, "in the earth and in Mūsā are signs for those who are certain"; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh said: "This is very far-fetched; the Qur'an is to be kept above the like of it." I say: the reason he finds it far-fetched is the distance between them, though the people of knowledge have done this in cases of greater distance. The third: that it is attached to an implied «جَعَلْنا», indicated by «وتَرَكْنا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or on His saying", meaning it may be conjoined to «وتَرَكْنا فيها آيةً» in the sense of: "and we made in Mūsā a sign", as in his saying:
4111 - فَعَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I fed her straw and cold water ...)
The Shaykh said: "There is no need to imply «وجَعَلْنا», for it is possible that the governor of the prepositional phrase be «وتَرَكْنا»." I say: al-Zamakhsharī meant only the first view, as the evidence of his saying: "«وفي موسى» is conjoined to «وفي الأرض» or to his saying «وتركْنا فيها»." He said "in the sense of" only from the side of explaining the meaning, not the grammar, and he made the verb overt only to point out that the two verbs differ. He means that this leaving is other than that leaving, and for that reason he brought it out with the root «الجَعْل» rather than the root «الترك», so that the difference would show.
His saying: {إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَاهُ}: Three views are permissible for this adverbial. The first: that it is accusative by «آية» on the first view, that is, "we left in the story of Mūsā a sign at the time of our sending him". The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «آية», that is, "a sign existing at the time of our sending". The third: that it is accusative by «تَرَكْنا».
His saying: {بِسُلْطَانٍ}: It is permissible that it be attached to the sending itself, and that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, either from Mūsā or from his pronoun, that is, "coupled with authority", which is the proof.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {بِرُكْنِهِ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تَوَلَّى».
His saying: {سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ}: «أو» here is in its usual sense of vagueness for the listener, or of doubt; he put himself, although he knew him to be a true prophet, in the position of one in doubt about his affair, to deceive his people. Abū ʿUbayda said: "«أو» has the sense of «و»." He said: "because he said both; Allah the Exalted said {إِنَّ هذا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ} [الأعراف: 109], and in another place {إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الذي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ} [الشعراء: 27]. And «أو» comes with the sense of «و», as in his saying:
4112 - أثَعْلَبَةَ الفوارِسَ أو رِياحا ... عَدَلْتَ بهم طُهَيَّةَ والخِشابا
(Did you set Ṭuhayya and al-Khishāb equal to Thaʿlaba the horsemen, or Riyāḥ?)"
People rejected this from him and said: no necessity calls for that; and as for the two verses, they do not indicate that he said both together, but only that he said both, which is more general than their being together, this at one time and that at another.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {وَجُنُودَهُ}: It is permissible that it be conjoined to the object of «أَخَذْناه», which is the apparent sense, and that it be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).
His saying: {وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. If it is a ḥāl from the object of «نَبَذْناهم», then the «واو» is necessary, since it contains no mention returning to the owner of the ḥāl; and if it is a ḥāl from the object of «أَخَذْناه», the «واو» is not obligatory, since the clause has a mention returning to it. It may be said: the pronoun in «نَبَذْناهم» refers to Pharaoh and his troops, so the ḥāl comes to have a mention returning to part of what the first pronoun included. There is room for objection in this, since it becomes like your saying: «جاء السلطانُ وجنوده فأكرمتُهم راكباً فرسَه» ("the sultan and his troops came, and I honoured them, riding his horse"), where you make «راكباً» a ḥāl from part of what the pronoun of «أكرمتُهم» included.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {وَفِي عَادٍ، وَفِي ثَمُودَ، وَفِي موسى}: the like of it was mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ جَعَلَتْهُ كالرميم}: this clause is in the position of the second object of «تَذَرُ», as if it were said: "it leaves nothing but made so", like «ما تركتُ زيداً إلاَّ عالماً» ("I left Zayd only as a scholar"). The Shaykh parsed it as a ḥāl (circumstantial), which is not clear.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {الصاعقة}: this is the reading of the majority. Al-Kisāʾī read «الصَّعْقَة», and al-Ḥasan «الصاقِعة». All of this was mentioned in al-Baqara.
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the object. «ينظرون» was said to be from «النظر» (looking), and also from «الانتظار» (waiting), that is, "they were awaiting the punishment promised them".

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ}: The two (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū ʿAmr read it with genitive on the «ميم»; the rest read it accusative. Abū al-Sammāl, Ibn Miqsam and Abū ʿAmr in the transmission of al-Aṣmaʿī read «وقومُ» nominative. As for the genitive, there are four views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «وفي الأرض». The second: that it is conjoined to «وفي موسى». The third: that it is conjoined to «وفي عاد». The fourth: that it is conjoined to «وفي ثمودَ», and this is the apparent one because of its nearness and the distance of the others. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else, for he said: "It was read with genitive in the sense of «وفي قوم نوح»." This is strengthened by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, «وفي قوم نوح». Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned only the last view because of its clarity.
As for the accusative, there are six views. The first: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is, «وأهلَكْنا قومَ نوح» ("and we destroyed the people of Nūḥ"), because what precedes indicates it. The second: that it is accusative by an implied «اذْكُرْ»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only these two. The third: that it is accusative as a conjunction on the object of «فأَخَذْناه». The fourth: that it is conjoined to the object of {فَنَبَذْنَاهُمْ فِي اليم}, and what fits this is that the people of Nūḥ were drowned before; but it is problematic, as they were not drowned in the sea (yamm), and the basis of conjunction is that it requires sharing in the attached elements. The fifth: that it is conjoined to the object of «فَأَخَذَتْهم الصاعقةُ»; and in it is a problem, because the thunderbolt did not seize them, rather they were destroyed by drowning, unless by «الصاعقة» is meant the calamity and great visitation of whatever kind, in which case it comes close. The sixth: that it is conjoined to the position of «وفي موسى»; Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it, and it is weak.
As for the nominative, it is as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with an implied khabar (predicate), that is, «أهلَكْناهم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The khabar is what comes after it", meaning His saying «إنهم كانوا قوماً فاسقين». It is not permissible that he mean His saying «من قبلُ», since the adverbial is incomplete and so cannot be predicated.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {والسمآء بَنَيْنَاهَا}: The majority read it accusative on the basis of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun); likewise His saying {والأرضَ فَرَشْناها}. The implied sense: «وبَنَيْنا السماءَ بَنَيْناها». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "that is, «ورفَعْنا السماءَ»", so he implied the governor from a wording other than the overt one; this is resorted to only when an implication that agrees in wording is impossible, as in «زيداً مررت به» and «زيداً ضربْتُ غلامَه». But in a case like «زيداً ضربتُه», only «ضربْتُ زيداً» is implied. Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn Miqsam read both nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar being what comes after them. The accusative is preferred because the clause of ishtighāl is conjoined to a verbal clause before it.
His saying: {بِأَيْدٍ}: It is permissible that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two views on it: the first, that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «بَنَيْناها», that is, "coupled with strength"; the second, that it is a ḥāl from its object, that is, "coupled with strength". It is also permissible that the «باء» be causal, that is, "by reason of our power"; and it is permissible that the «باء» be figuratively one of instrument, by making «الأَيْد» like the tool with which one builds, as in your saying «بَنَيْتُ بيتَك بالآجُرِّ» ("I built your house with brick").
His saying: {وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ}: It is permissible that the clause be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «بَنَيْناها», and permissible that it be a ḥāl from its object; the object of «مُوْسِعون» is omitted, that is, "extending its structure". It is also permissible that no object be implied for it, because its meaning is «لَقادِرون» ("able"), from your saying «ما في وُسْعي كذا», that is, "it is not within my capacity and strength."

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {فَنِعْمَ الماهدون}: the one specified for praise is omitted because the meaning is understood, that is, «نحن» ("we"), as in His saying {نِعْمَ العبد} [ص: 44].

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ}: It is permissible that it be attached to «خَلَقْنا», that is, "we created from everything two kinds"; and that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «زوجَيْن», because originally it is an adjective of it, the implied sense being "we created two kinds, existing from everything". The first is stronger in meaning.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: There are two views. The more apparent: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "the matter is like that". The pointing by «ذلك» is, al-Zamakhsharī said, "to their denial of the Messenger and calling him a sorcerer and a madman", then he explained what he had stated in general by "«ما أَتى»". The second: that the «كاف» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); Makkī said this and did not make clear its implied form. It is not valid for it to be accusative by what comes after it, because of the negative «ما». As for the meaning, it is not impossible, and for that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not valid for the «كاف» to be accusative by «أتى», because the negative «ما» does not allow what follows it to govern what precedes it; had it been «لم يأتِ», it would have been valid." He means that if «لم» had come in place of «ما», it would be permissible for the «كاف» to be accusative by «أتى», because the meaning allows it. The implied sense: "Quraysh denied with a denial like the denial of the earlier nations of their messengers." This is indicated by His saying {مَآ أَتَى الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ} to the end of the verse.
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَالُواْ}: the clause of saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from {الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ}, and «من رسولٍ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «أتى»; as if it were said: "No messenger came to the earlier ones except while they said: He is a sorcerer." The pronoun in «به» refers to the saying indicated by «قالوا», that is, "Did the earlier and the later ones bequeath this saying to one another, containing 'sorcerer or madman'?" The interrogative is for amazement.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ}: attached to «خَلَقْتُ». There was disagreement over the jinn and mankind: is the intent general, the meaning being "except to command them to worship and to have them acknowledge it"? This is reported from ʿAlī. Or the meaning is "to obey me and submit to my decree", so the believer does that willingly and the disbeliever unwillingly. Or the meaning is "except as prepared for worship", and then among them some can do it and some cannot, as in your saying «هذا القلمُ بَرَيْتُه للكتابة» ("I trimmed this pen for writing"), after which you may write with it or may not. Or the intent is specific, and the meaning is: "I did not create the jinn and the believing humans". It was also said: "the obedient". The first is best.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {أَن يُطْعِمُونِ}: It was said that a muḍāf is omitted in it, that is, "that they feed my creation". It was also said that the meaning is "that they benefit me", and the expression used one of the forms of benefit, because it is the habit of masters to benefit from their servants, while Allah, glorified and exalted, is free of need of that.

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {المتين}: The majority read it nominative. There are several views: either a naʿt (adjective) of «الرزَّاق», or a naʿt of «ذو», or a naʿt of the ism of «إنَّ» by position, which is the school of al-Jarmī, al-Farrāʾ and others, or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. On every assumption it is emphasis, because «ذو القوة» gives the same benefit. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «الرازق», as he read «وَفِي السمآء رازِقُكُمْ», as mentioned. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash read «المتينِ» genitive; it was said: an adjective of «القوة», and its adjective was made masculine because its feminine is not a true feminine. It was also said: because it has the sense of «الأَيْد». Ibn Jinnī said: "It is genitive by proximity, as in their saying «هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» ("this is the hole of a ruined lizard")", meaning that it is an adjective of a nominative word and was made genitive only because it neighboured a genitive. This is the less preferred view because another is possible, and proximity is not resorted to except in need.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {ذَنُوباً}: «الذَّنوب» originally is the bucket filled with water. In the hadith: «فأتى بذَنوبٍ من ماءٍ» ("then he was brought a bucket of water"). If it is not full, it is a «دَلْو»; then it was used to express a share. Alqama said:
4113 - وفي كلِّ حَيٍّ قد خبَطْتُ بنِعْمَةٍ ... فحُقَّ لشاسٍ مِنْ نَداكَ ذَنوبُ
(In every tribe I have dispensed a favour, so a share of your generosity is due to Shās.)
In the paucal plural it is «أَذْنِبة», and in the plural of abundance «ذَنائب». When this verse was recited, the king said: "Yes, and «أَذْنِبَة»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الذَّنوب» is the large bucket. This is a figure of speech, its origin being among water-drawers who share the water, so this one has a bucket and that one has a bucket. The rajaz poet said:
4114 - لنا ذَنوبٌ ولكم ذَنُوبُ ... فإنْ أَبَيْتُمْ فلنا القَليبُ
(We have a bucket and you have a bucket; if you refuse, then the well is ours.)
Al-Rāghib said: «الذَّنوب» is the bucket that has a tail (dhanab)." End. He thereby took account of the derivation. «الذَّنوب» is also a horse with a long tail, which is an attribute on the pattern «فَعُوْل»; and «الذَّنوب» is the meat of the lower back. It is said: «يومٌ ذَنوبٌ», that is, a day of long evil, by metaphor from that.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {الذي يُوعَدُونَ}: the returning pronoun is omitted, because its conditions are fulfilled, that is, «يُوْعَدُونه».
